exercise1.prompt: Missing Values: Drop the incomplete rows

hiddenCases.name: the original list is not modified

exercise1.hint: Build a new list rather than removing from the one you were given. Removing while looping skips rows, and a caller who still needs their data will not thank you.

exercise2.prompt: Missing Values: Fill with the mean

hiddenCases.name: the mean uses only the known values, not zeros
the mean is rounded to one place
the caller's list is not changed

exercise2.hint: known = [s for s in scores if s is not None]. If known is empty, return the list. Otherwise compute mean = round(sum(known) / len(known), 1) and build [mean if s is None else s for s in scores].

questions.prompt: What does filling missing scores with the average do to the average?
choices: Leaves it the same but makes the spread look smaller
questions.explain: Every filled row sits exactly at the mean, so the mean does not move and the data looks less varied than it is.

questions.prompt: Why is removing items from a list while looping over it a bug?
choices: The loop skips the item after each removal
questions.explain: Removing shifts everything left while the loop moves right, so every removal steps over its neighbour.

questions.prompt: When is dropping rows with missing values reasonable?
choices: The missing column is the one you are analysing
Most of the file is missing that column
You need the row count to stay the same
questions.explain: Dropping most of your data is not cleaning, it is selecting. If the column is mostly missing, that fact is the finding.

questions.prompt: Filling a missing test score with 0 claims what?
choices: That the student sat the test and scored nothing
That the row should be ignored
questions.explain: A fill value is a statement about the world. Zero is the right fill only when zero is what actually happened.
